subject: Fleet choreography: proposed resize window and commit trigger
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@asterionlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fleet choreography: proposed resize window and commit trigger

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for taking time yesterday. Based on the Q2 usage snapshot you shared and our conversation, I sketched a low-friction plan to align your Dedicated fleet size to observed utilization while preserving runway for peak experiments. High-level proposal is attached (proposal-draft-v2.pdf).

Key points:
- Current steady-state: ~320 steady rGPU-hours/day (prefix-heavy inference), 95th percentile latency target 120ms.
- Recent peaks: short 3–6 hour bursts reaching ~620 rGPU-hours driven by nightly batch reranks and A/B evals.
- Suggested path: 10% immediate top-up (capacity buffer for A/B), 20% conditional tranche after a two-week monitoring window if utilization stays above 70% for rolling 7-day windows.

Operational mechanics ("fleet choreography"):
1) Short window autoscaling: enable burst pool with pre-warmed nodes (config attached) to cover the 95th->99th percentile spikes without long cold-starts.
2) Commit trigger: if rolling 7-day avg utilization > 70% AND peak-to-mean ratio < 2.0, initiate tranche-add (monthly billing amendment) to add 12 GPUs.
3) Fallbacks: route non-latency-critical batch jobs to a queued burst tier or scheduled overnight windows to reduce persistent commit needs.

Ben and Marissa are copied for sizing validation and contract language. The attached runbook (runbook-fleet-choreography.md) lays out exact autoscaling settings, warm pool sizing, and monitoring alerts we recommend.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm whether the overnight rerank window is flexible?
- If yes, we can cut the suggested committed add from 12 GPUs -> 8 GPUs and rely on burst for the remainder.

I can update the proposal and generate an amendment draft for procurement once you confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: proposal-draft-v2.pdf, runbook-fleet-choreography.md

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@asterionlabs.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet choreography: proposed resize window and commit trigger

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan and the two docs. A few clarifications from Asterion side:
- Overnight rerank jobs are somewhat flexible; we can move up to 60% of the nightly work into a scheduled window that starts at 1:00 AM PT, but some experiments still need same-day completion.
- Our Q2 CSV (attached) shows that experimental traffic is concentrated Tue-Thu; the two-week window you suggested would need to be aware of that cadence.
- Procurement will want an option that minimizes committed spend but preserves predictable latency. Can you give two scenarios: (A) conservative commit (8 GPUs) + burst, (B) aggressive commit (12 GPUs) and eliminate most nightly bursts? Please show estimated monthly run-rate delta for both.

Also looped in procurement (procurement@asterionlabs.ai) in case they want to run the numbers in parallel.

Thanks —
Sofia Martinez
Head of Product Infrastructure, Asterion Labs

Date: 2027-07-17T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet choreography: proposed resize window and commit trigger

Sofia / Karthik —

Quick sizing note from infra: the split scenarios look like this (ballpark, we can tighten once you sign off on the monitoring window):

Scenario A (conservative commit)
- Add 8 committed GPUs (A100-class equivalent), enable burst pool sized for an extra 10 GPUs for 6-hour daily peaks.
- Expected monthly delta vs current: ~$14,200 (commit incremental amortized) + burst incremental egress/short-run costs ~ $1,800 (variable).
- Latency: preserves 95th percentile target for steady traffic; brief degradation risk only if bursts exceed warm pool capacity.

Scenario B (aggressive commit)
- Add 12 committed GPUs, reduce burst pool to 4 GPUs.
- Expected monthly delta: ~$20,900 (commit) + burst ~$600.
- Latency: most experiments will get same-day completion on dedicated capacity; lowers variable tail risk.

Operational caveats:
- If you keep the two-week monitor but traffic spikes are front-loaded in that window (Tue-Thu), our trigger should evaluate a weighted 7-day average (we recommend weighting recent 48 hours at 1.5x to avoid delaying a necessary commit).
- We can implement a soft commit: start billing at next invoice but hold physical provisioning for 7 days to allow you to cancel with minimal penalty if utilization collapses (<45% for the 7-day window).

I'll attach a short cost model (CSV) to the HubSpot deal and update the proposal. Marissa — if procurement wants the exact amendment text we should prepare the two-option addendum.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@asterionlabs.ai>, Procurement <procurement@asterionlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet choreography: proposed resize window and commit trigger

Sofia / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick feedback and the Q2 CSV. Attached is a two-option summary (proposal-draft-v2.pdf updated) and a short amendment template for procurement to review. TL;DR:

Option A — conservative: 8 committed GPUs + burst pool (10 GPUs)
- Monthly expected delta: ~$16k (includes amortized commit + expected burst).
- Pros: lower committed spend, flexible runway.
- Cons: slightly higher variability in peak tails.

Option B — aggressive: 12 committed GPUs, burst pool (4 GPUs)
- Monthly expected delta: ~$21.5k
- Pros: more predictable latency and capacity for experiments.
- Cons: higher fixed cost.

Operational guardrails we propose to include in the amendment:
- 14-day observation window after enablement during which either party can request a one-time adjustment before billing takes effect.
- Monitoring and alerts: autopilot will send utilization and warm-pool fill-rate reports daily to the shared Slack channel and create a weekly digest to your SREs.
- Soft-commit option (pay-as-you-warm): billing begins at next invoice but provisioning delayed 7 days; cancelable if weighted 7-day utilization < 45%.

If procurement is happy with the language, I will prepare the DocuSign flow and a billing addendum. Can procurement confirm preferred option and whether Asterion legal needs any additional SLAs on warm-pool startup time?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposal-draft-v2.pdf (updated), asterion_usage_report_q2.csv, runbook-fleet-choreography.md
